title: GE to break up into 3 companies focusing on aviation, health care and energy
主要内容: General Electric (GE) announced plans to split into three separate companies, each focusing on aviation, health care, and energy. The decision, made public on November 9, 2021, aims to enhance focus, capital allocation, and strategic flexibility for each unit. The health-care unit is set to be spun off by early 2023, while the energy unit will follow by early 2024. GE shares rose over 2% on the day of the announcement, despite a broader market pullback. CEO Lawrence Culp emphasized the benefits of creating industry-leading public companies, stating that the move would allow each unit to better serve customers and investors. The company has been struggling with underperformance over the past two decades, losing 2% annually since 2009 compared to the S&P 500's 9% return. The spinoffs are expected to incur about $2 billion in transaction and operational costs, with the energy segment anticipated to have the least debt. GE plans to use proceeds from the recent sale of its aviation financing unit to reduce its debt, which is expected to total less than $65 billion by the end of 2021.
